headline: Dhaka launches automated traffic signal system at Shahbagh to cut congestion
summary: The Dhaka South City Corporation has introduced a tech-driven signal system on a trial basis, with plans to expand to 50 key intersections across the capital.
details: An automated traffic signal system has been launched on a trial basis at the Shahbagh intersection in Dhaka to modernize traffic management and reduce chronic congestion.
The system was inaugurated by Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Abdus Salam, with technical assistance provided by the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET).
The pilot project will initially cover 20 key intersections, with eight already prepared including Banglamotor, Kakrail Circle, and the InterContinental Hotel area.
Authorities aim to expand the modern signal system to another 50 important intersections across Dhaka within the next few months, including 22 more under the DSCC.
Once fully operational, the automated system is expected to significantly reduce the need for traffic police to manually control signals at these busy junctions.
Administrator Salam emphasized that the technology's success depends on public compliance with traffic laws, urging motorists to avoid illegal parking and road obstructions.
caption:
Dhaka is going automated! A new smart traffic system debuts at Shahbagh to fight the city's chronic congestion.

An automated traffic signal system has been launched on a trial basis at the Shahbagh intersection in Dhaka to modernize traffic management and reduce chronic congestion.

The system was inaugurated by Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) Administrator Abdus Salam, with technical assistance provided by the Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET).

The pilot project will initially cover 20 key intersections, with eight already prepared including Banglamotor, Kakrail Circle, and the InterContinental Hotel area.

Authorities aim to expand the modern signal system to another 50 important intersections across Dhaka within the next few months, including 22 more under the DSCC.

Once fully operational, the automated system is expected to significantly reduce the need for traffic police to manually control signals at these busy junctions.

Administrator Salam emphasized that the technology's success depends on public compliance with traffic laws, urging motorists to avoid illegal parking and road obstructions.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud's [[6-wicket haul destroys Australia]] in Darwin
headline: Hasan Mahmud's 6-wicket haul destroys Australia in Darwin
summary: Bangladesh bowl out Australia for 198 on Day 1 of the first Test, with Hasan Mahmud claiming a historic career-best 6/55.
details: Bangladesh dominated the opening day of the first Test against Australia at Marrara Stadium in Darwin, bowling out the hosts for 198.
Hasan Mahmud delivered a masterclass, claiming career-best figures of 6 for 55, becoming the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a Test five-wicket haul in Australia.
Steve Smith was the only significant resistance, scoring 71 runs, but he eventually fell to Hasan Mahmud in the third session.
Smith later admitted in a post-match press conference that he had nicked a delivery from Ebadot Hossain early on, but was saved by the technology (Real Time Snicko) which showed no disturbance.
At stumps on Day 1, Bangladesh were comfortably in control at 96 for 1, trailing by 102 runs with nine wickets in hand.
The Tigers' fast-bowling unit earned widespread praise for their consistency and discipline throughout the first innings.
caption:
A historic day for the Tigers! Hasan Mahmud takes 6 wickets to bowl out Australia for 198.

Bangladesh dominated the opening day of the first Test against Australia at Marrara Stadium in Darwin, bowling out the hosts for 198.

Hasan Mahmud delivered a masterclass, claiming career-best figures of 6 for 55, becoming the first Bangladeshi bowler to take a Test five-wicket haul in Australia.

Steve Smith was the only significant resistance, scoring 71 runs, but he eventually fell to Hasan Mahmud in the third session.

Smith later admitted in a post-match press conference that he had nicked a delivery from Ebadot Hossain early on, but was saved by the technology (Real Time Snicko) which showed no disturbance.

At stumps on Day 1, Bangladesh were comfortably in control at 96 for 1, trailing by 102 runs with nine wickets in hand.

The Tigers' fast-bowling unit earned widespread praise for their consistency and discipline throughout the first innings.
